text.tspan: A data pipeline that runs once per city, and a static web app that calls Amazon Location Service live. One AWS Region: us-west-2.
Registry of Open Data on AWS
Amazon S3, public buckets, no account needed
Read only the city's bounding box
DuckDB + rasterio, HTTP range requests, 34 s
Runs on a laptop: 2.1 s of compute per city
Every push runs the tests, a secret scan and Terraform checks;
Figures are in the HTML, so the page
Warns if someone abuses the public API
MapLibre GL JS + h3-js draw the hexagons, refuges and proposals.
Personal search: type an address, tap the map or use your location.
Only the person's search goes to Amazon Location. No accounts, cookies or analytics;
API key restricted to the site's domain. Results used once (SingleUse), never stored.
The pipeline reads only each city's bounding box from the open-data buckets on Amazon S3.
It writes small static files, plus the page text with every figure, generated from stats.json.
GitHub Actions tests the code and deploys it to AWS Amplify with a short-lived IAM role (OIDC).
Amplify serves the site over a CDN with HTTPS.
Amazon Location Maps draws the base map.
Places geocodes the person's address and finds cool places nearby.
Routes draws the area reachable on foot and the walking route to the nearest refuge.
